PC: Apply monitor and verbalize vital sign abnormalities of hyperthermia, tachycardia, tachypnea, and hypoxia
Perform a physical exam and verbalize the findings of goiter, agitation, sweating, respiratory distress, rales on pulmonary auscultation
Ask the patient’s family member what events led up to the current presentation, the patient’s medical and surgical history, allergies, medications, and family history.
Apply a nonrebreather mask either by asking the RN to do so, or by personally doing so, and start flow rate of at least 10L/min
Prepare intubation equipment including both direct and/or video assisted options
Request a chest radiograph, and verbalize the finding of pulmonary edema
Request an EKG, and verbalize the finding of atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
Perform POCUS of heart, lungs, and IVC, and verbalize the findings of a hyperdynamic heart, pulmonary edema, and high output heart failure.
Order labs including, but not limited to, CBC, BMP, BNP, blood gas, TSH and TFTs, and verbalize the finding of an elevated BNP

Administer medical treatment including propylthiouracil (PTU) 300 mg – 1000 mg PO, propranolol 0.5 – 2mg IV or 20-80mg PO/NG, or esmolol 250 – 500 mcg/kg IV, dexamethasone 2mg IV or hydrocortisone 100mg IV1
SBP: Consult/discuss with maternal-fetal medicine the management of thyroid storm in a post-partum patient
